supporting_observations.claim: WS-LMARTINS-01 made recurring connections to 10.40.20.30:8080, the inventoried explicit proxy, at 13:36:11, 13:41:10, 13:46:05, 13:51:18, 13:55:49, and 14:00:52 UTC. These records support approximately five-minute periodicity.

Those six connections have similar traffic volumes: 9,556–9,794 originating bytes and 43,489–43,590 responding bytes. This establishes a repeated traffic pattern, but does not distinguish legitimate polling from malicious beaconing.

The recurring connection records identify only the workstation-to-proxy leg and label its service as HTTP. They do not identify the external destination, HTTPS CONNECT target, request content, user, or originating executable; therefore they cannot establish either malicious communication or attribution to the approved PixelForge updater.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status metadata reports that WS-LMARTINS-01 winsec and Sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, preventing process attribution during the alerted interval. This metadata has no record ID.

The supplied collection-status metadata reports that PROXY-NWD-01 proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, preventing recovery of external destinations and inspected requests from the provided proxy evidence. This metadata has no record ID.

Although Zeek DNS and SSL coverage is reported as operational, no supplied DNS or SSL record identifies an external destination for the recurring proxy connections. The connection records themselves expose only 10.40.20.30:8080 (T035-00088, T035-00117, T035-00235, T035-00263, T035-00274, T035-00284).
claims_not_established: Whether the recurring connections reached updates.pixelforge-suite.com or any other external destination.
Whether pfupdater.exe, another legitimate application, or a malicious process initiated the recurring connections.
Whether the alerted traffic carried command-and-control messages, exfiltrated data, or legitimate update checks.
Whether the observed workstation-to-proxy connections used HTTPS tunnels beyond the proxy.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover proxy logs or upstream connection records for the recurring sessions, correlating workstation source ports 52139, 56639, 58821, 53928, 54936, and 56858 with external destinations and CONNECT targets.
Recover endpoint network/process telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC to identify the initiating executable, command line, user, parent process, and executable signature/hash.
Obtain PixelForge updater logs and installed-software evidence to test whether approved update checks account for these specific sessions.
Review retained packet captures, proxy egress TLS metadata, or inspected request logs for the identified sessions to determine their purpose.
